review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the definitions it depends on: copyCount, copyEdgeLoad, triangleDegree, card_completeGraph, earlyDensity and earlyTemplateScale. I also grepped the repository for uses of the scale and density definitions. The two @[simp] lemmas, triangle_copyCount and triangle_copyEdgeLoad, have specific left-hand sides on the local triangleRequired. I saw no cycle, competing rule or unwanted expansion, so I made no claim about those. The findings are about missing canonical simp lemmas for earlyDensity at 0 and for the triangle scale definitions. Both are supported by repeated manual unfolding in this file and in other files. I could not run Lean. Whether the proposed simp lemmas would fire cleanly, and whether they would clash with existing simp sets elsewhere, is therefore unchecked.

findings.problem: `earlyDensity n 0` has no canonical simp lemma. Every use at index 0 unfolds the definition and then runs `simp only [Nat.cast_zero, mul_zero, zero_div, sub_zero]` by hand. This file does it at lines 66 and 92, and CodegreeVertexCount repeats it. Other files re-prove `earlyDensity n 0 = 1-1/(n : ℝ)` with an ad hoc `simp [earlyDensity]`. The normal form is never recorded as a lemma, and unfolding the definition exposes the `6*(0:ℝ)/n^2` junk term each time.
findings.proposed_change: Next to `earlyDensity` (or at the top of this file), add `@[simp] lemma earlyDensity_zero (n : ℕ) : earlyDensity n 0 = 1 - 1/(n : ℝ)`. The proof is `by simp [earlyDensity]`, which is the proof already used in BalancedJump. Then the manual `simp only [earlyDensity, Nat.cast_zero, …]` calls reduce to `simp` or `rw [earlyDensity_zero]`. The scattered `have he : earlyDensity n 0 = 1-1/(n : ℝ)` blocks can go.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical form for the density at time 0, and the definition is no longer unfolded just to clean up a zero cast. The same ad hoc rewrite stops being repeated in 5 or more places, so proofs are shorter and easier to maintain.

findings.excerpt: have hs : earlyTriangleScale n 0 = ((n : ℝ)-1)^3/6 := by
findings.problem: `earlyTriangleScale` and `triangleNoiseLoad` are plain defs with no unfolding or evaluation lemmas. The closed form at index 0 is proved only as a local `have hs`. The relation `earlyTriangleScale n i = earlyTemplateScale 3 3 n i / 6` is re-established by `unfold`/`simpa only [earlyTriangleScale, mul_div_assoc]` in `earlyTriangleScale_regular` (lines 54 and 56). It is again re-derived by unfolding in TriangleNoiseJumpBudget and EdgeStabilityRate. Without a simp-friendly equation, each consumer unfolds through `earlyTemplateScale` and `earlyDensity` and then cleans up with `field_simp` or `ring`, and the form it reaches depends on how it unfolds.
findings.proposed_change: Add equation lemmas next to the defs, for example `lemma earlyTriangleScale_eq (n i : ℕ) : earlyTriangleScale n i = (n : ℝ)^3 * earlyDensity n i ^ 3 / 6 := rfl`. Add `@[simp] lemma earlyTriangleScale_zero {n : ℕ} : earlyTriangleScale n 0 = ((n : ℝ)-1)^3/6`, which is the content of `hs` under the same hypotheses. Add the matching `triangleNoiseLoad_eq`. Then initial_triangle_relative_error can `rw [earlyTriangleScale_zero]`, and the later files can rewrite instead of unfolding.
findings.benefit: The normal form of the triangle scale is stated once and the abstraction is not repeatedly broken. The `hs`-style computation is reusable, and downstream proofs about `earlyTriangleScale n 0` no longer redo the unfold-and-field_simp step.
